headline: Calcutta HC dismisses Service Tax appeal under s.35G; valuation/rate issues lie before Supreme Court
reference: Commissioner of Service Tax-II (now Commissioner of CGST & CX, Kolkata South) vs M/S Alfa Aluminium Private Limited, CEXA/48/2026, Calcutta High Court, 12 October 2026
summary_points: Issue: Department appealed under s.35G of the Central Excise Act read with s.83 of the Finance Act against a CESTAT order on composition scheme and Rule 2A valuation.
Questions raised included mandatory option under the composition scheme, Rule 2A valuation, extended limitation, penalties and the Interarch remand.
Held: Under ss.35G and 35L, the appeal should be preferred before the Supreme Court under s.35L(2); the High Court dismissed the department's appeal.
Impact: Disputes on valuation or rate of duty/tax from the Tribunal are not maintainable before the High Court; the Supreme Court is the forum.
The order does not decide the merits of the composition scheme or limitation questions.
who_is_affected: Service tax and central excise litigants, departmental officers and advisers handling Tribunal orders involving valuation or rate-related questions.
action_required: Check whether the Tribunal order relates to valuation or rate before choosing the forum, and file in the Supreme Court under s.35L where applicable, within limitation.

In Commissioner of Service Tax-II (now CGST & CX, Kolkata South) vs M/S Alfa Aluminium Private Limited (CEXA/48/2026, 12 October 2026), the Department filed an appeal under Section 35G of the Central Excise Act, 1944 read with Section 83 of the Finance Act.

The proposed questions covered the composition scheme option, Rule 2A valuation, extended limitation, penalties and a remand based on the Supreme Court's Interarch Building Products ruling.

The Division Bench of Justices Rajarshi Bharadwaj and Sudip Deb did not go into the merits. Reading Sections 35G and 35L together, it held the appeal should be preferred before the Supreme Court under Section 35L(2), and dismissed the Department's appeal.

Takeaway: where a Tribunal order relates to valuation or rate, check the correct appellate forum before filing, as the wrong choice can cost time.

Please verify with the official source or full order before relying on this update.
